description: Monotonic descending sweep of valid two-head latent widths below the retained d=14 architecture.
proposal: Family: attention organization. Retained incumbent is 3528 parameters at 99.660000%, a +0.660000 percentage-point margin over 99%. Same-family history: accepted attempt-0006 at d=14 (3528, 99.66%); no scored failure; 1 prior attempt. Hypothesis: the retained d=14 two-head representation may tolerate additional even-width compression while retaining two independent attention pathways. This is a parameterization-preserving latent-width compression, not a representational substitution. Ordering: test d_model values 12, 10, 8, 6, 4, 2 in descending order with n_heads=2 and ff=20 fixed. Acceptance/rollback: the runner retains only a qualified smaller candidate and restores the incumbent otherwise; stop on any scored discard/error because smaller widths are then ineligible under the declared monotonic policy. Stopping: first discard/error, no eligible widths, or six micro-trials. Maximum micro-trials: 6. Compute budget: at most 180000 training steps and six configured runner windows (21600 seconds); no training, verification, retention, or silent discarding occurs outside run_attempt.py. This is more informative than skipping to d=10 because d=12 is the nearest untested valid two-head decrement.
summary: Attempted the declared two-head latent-width range beginning at d=12. The first micro-trial was an optimization failure: it completed 30000 steps in 8.3 minutes but validation peaked at 7.6%, never produced a checkpoint, and consequently had no official score. No candidate was retained; frontier remains d=14, ff=20 at 3528 parameters and 99.660000%. Compute used: 30000 training steps. Stopped because the scored error changed the monotonic lower-width eligibility rule; d=10, 8, 6, 4, and 2 were not run.
